name: Herod Agrippa
charge: Accepting worship due to God alone
summary: Arrayed in royal robes, the king gave an oration and the crowd shouted that his was the voice of a god, not a man. He accepted the acclaim. The judgment was immediate and public.
offense: The sin was not the speech but the silence after it: he took to himself the honor owed to God, receiving worship he should have refused as Paul and Barnabas had refused it at Lystra.
judgment: Immediately an angel of the Lord struck him because he gave not God the glory; he was eaten of worms and died. The contrast follows at once: but the word of God grew and multiplied.

entries.commentary: Behold my servant whom I uphold, my elect in whom my soul delighteth; the Most High put his spirit upon him and he shall bring forth judgment to the gentiles. This goes into Christ, who shall not cry nor lift up nor cause his voice to be heard in the street. A bruised reed he shall not break and the smoking flax he shall not quench; he shall bring forth judgment unto truth. He shall not fail nor be discouraged till he has set judgment in the earth, and the isles shall wait for his law. -

Thus saith God the Lord, he that created the heavens and stretched them out, that spread forth the earth, that giveth breath unto the people upon it and spirit to them that walk therein. I the Lord have called thee in righteousness and will hold thine hand and keep thee, and give thee for a covenant of the people, for a light of the gentiles, to open the blind eyes, to bring out the prisoners from the prison and them that sit in darkness out of the prison house. I am the Lord, that is my name, and my glory will I not give to another nor my praise to graven images. He declares the end from the beginning: before the new things spring forth he tells them to you.

Sing unto the Lord a new song and his praise from the end of the earth, ye that go down to the sea and the isles and the inhabitants thereof. Let the wilderness and the cities, the villages of Kedar, and the inhabitants of the rock lift up their voice and shout from the top of the mountains, giving glory unto the Lord. The Lord shall go forth as a mighty man and stir up jealousy like a man of war; he shall cry, yea roar, and prevail against his enemies.

I have long time held my peace, been still and refrained myself, but now will I cry like a travailing woman and destroy and devour at once. The Most High holds back because all the prophecies in this bible must be fulfilled, and once that happens it is going down. I will make waste mountains and hills, dry up the herbs, and make the rivers islands. I will bring the blind by a way they knew not, make darkness light before them and crooked things straight, and not forsake them. They shall be turned back and greatly ashamed that trust in graven images, that say to the molten images, ye are our gods. -

Hear ye deaf and look ye blind that ye may see; who is blind but my servant, or deaf as my messenger that I sent? The Lord is well pleased for his righteousness' sake and will magnify the law and make it honorable. This is why Christ came magnifying the law: ye heard it said thou shalt not commit adultery, but whoever looks on a woman to lust after her has committed adultery already; and when they questioned him on divorce he said in the beginning it was not so.

But this is a people robbed and spoiled, all of them snared in holes and hidden in prison houses; they are for a prey and none delivereth, a spoil and none saith restore. This is talking about us the Israelites: the other nations come and set up in our communities, sell their goods, and take the money back, preying on us and spoiling us like the spoils of war. Who among you will give ear to this? Who gave Jacob for a spoil and Israel to the robbers? Did not the Lord, he against whom we have sinned, for they would not walk in his ways nor be obedient to his law. Therefore he poured upon him the fury of his anger and the strength of battle, and it set him on fire round about, yet he knew not, and it burned him, yet he laid it not to heart. We were consumed for our sins on the slave ships but laid it not to heart, not considering that the Most High punished us and brought us over to turn us back to our maker.

An image in itself is not the sin, except for that white image of the beast; making images to bow down to them and serve them is the transgression, for the Lord thy God is a jealous God. Visiting the iniquity of the fathers upon the children unto the third and fourth generation: Israel is yet this day in captivity, scattered for a reproach and a curse, according to all the iniquities of the fathers which departed from the Lord. Right now Israel is paying for the sins of the fathers; that is why the people are scattered to the four corners of the earth.

And shewing mercy unto thousands of them that love me, and keep my commandments. Judith recounted how the Most High tried the fathers for the examination of their hearts: he tried Abraham and Isaac, and Jacob in Mesopotamia of Syria keeping the sheep of Laban, serving twenty years with his wages changed and given Leah when he looked for Rachel. In Judith's day there was no tribe, family, people, nor city that worshipped gods made with hands, as had been aforetime; for that cause she trusted the Lord would not despise the nation. Mercy rests on them that know none other God, not Allah, not Buddha, not a white Jesus.

Remember the Sabbath day, to keep it holy. The word says remember because Israel would forget it: in this captivity the people were forced to serve other gods and their religions, and the Sabbath was lost through forced conversion. Look up the blue laws, also known as Sunday laws; they help give understanding of why the Bible says remember the Sabbath day.

An altar of stone was not to be built of hewn stone, for lifting up a tool upon it pollutes it; neither go up by steps unto the altar, that thy nakedness be not discovered thereon. This scripture helps explain pants, precept upon precept. The priests were given linen breeches to cover their nakedness from the loins even unto the thighs when they came near the altar, and Israel was called in this same reading to be a kingdom of priests, so do not be simple and say that law was only for Aaron and his sons. Those breeches were made for men and not for women, as the law of the garments also shows.
